title: [Power Display] Module only detects first enumerated monitor; subsequent monitors ignored

judgment.rationale: The original report provides a useful four-display/unplug sequence and the issue timeline links a related Nvidia-monitor report, but the pinned source now enumerates each returned monitor and the report is from 0.99.1. A fresh reproduction is needed to tell whether discovery still fails or the display topology differs.
evidence: The report says the flyout and Settings list showed only the Wisecoco and one of three Dell U2725QE displays, then one Dell after unplugging the Wisecoco.
The timeline links #50882, a separate monitor-detection report involving Nvidia.
The current PowerDisplay refresh path uses DiscoverMonitorsAsync and UpdateMonitorList adds every non-hidden discovered monitor.
judgment.recommended_action: Request one current diagnostic capture and topology screenshot after the exact unplug/replug sequence; do not infer a duplicate from the related issue.

fix_assessment.rationale: The pinned source already iterates all discovered monitors. No new enumeration fix is grounded until a current report shows which monitors Windows and PowerToys each expose.

issue_context.summary: The reporter says Power Display showed only one of four connected monitors and continued to show only one Dell after unplugging the first display.
known_information: The reported topology includes three Dell U2725QE displays and one Wisecoco HDMI display.
The reporter describes an unplug/replug repro and a related Nvidia monitor-detection report is linked.
inferences: The missing outputs may be specific to the current monitor/driver topology; the related issue does not prove a shared defect.
The pinned source may have evolved since 0.99.1; no shipped fix is inferred.
issue_context.analysis: The report is detailed enough to repeat but not to distinguish a PowerToys enumeration fault from Windows display discovery. Ask for current evidence after the exact sequence and compare the OS display list with the module list.
initial_investigation: Read the full issue and comments; the latest comment says the reporter suspected a driver but dccutil showed the monitor was working.
Read src/modules/PowerDisplay/PowerDisplay/ViewModels/MainViewModel.Monitors.cs: RefreshMonitorsAsync calls DiscoverMonitorsAsync and UpdateMonitorList iterates each returned monitor.
Read src/modules/PowerDisplay/PowerDisplay/PowerDisplayXAML/MainWindow.xaml: monitor content is bound to the view-model monitor collection.

information_gaps.information: A fresh report after the four-monitor topology is connected and after the Wisecoco unplug/replug sequence, plus confirmation of the current PowerToys version.
information_gaps.why_needed: The pinned source calls DiscoverMonitorsAsync and adds each returned monitor, while the original report says the flyout and Settings list expose only a subset. A fresh capture can distinguish current discovery failure from monitor-driver/topology behavior.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Repeat the supplied four-monitor and unplug/replug sequence on the current release, then immediately add a comment containing /bugreport. Include a screenshot of Windows Display Settings showing all four displays and the exact PowerToys version.

actions.label: Recheck monitor discovery on current build

comment.body: Thanks for providing the four-monitor topology and the unplug/replug sequence. The current source adds each monitor returned by discovery, so please retest on the current PowerToys release and compare the set shown in Windows Display Settings with the Power Display list. If the mismatch remains, include that screenshot and a fresh comment containing `/bugreport` immediately after the sequence; this will show whether Windows and PowerToys disagree about the same display set.
